name: Reverse Hyperextension
research: No high bench prop, so a 0.45 x 0.95 x 1.0 m box is the 'high bench' (y -1.05..-0.10, top z 1.0). Face down: root rot X +90 (head toward -Y). Chest front ~0.18 m ahead of the pelvis joint -> root z 1.0+0.18 = 1.18, y 0; hip joints = root + Rx(90)(+-0.11,-0.051,0.003) = (+-0.11,-0.003,1.129), 0.097 m past the box end so the thigh front (~0.08) clears the end face. Start: legs 15 deg behind vertical, 0.88 m hip-ankle -> ankle (0.13,0.225,0.279); foot rot X 30 (neutral for that leg tilt is 15, +15 pointed) -> toe tip ~0.13 above floor. End: legs level, ankle (0.13,0.877,1.14) = 1 cm above the hip line; foot rot X 120 = toes pointing back/down, pointed. Knee pole: anterior faces -Y when hanging, -Z when level. Hands hold the box sides: upper arm elev 105 / plane 80 (down and toward the head), elbow 95, forearm folds up (bend_world up) so the hand sits at the side near the top edge, no prop. Lawrence 2019 (hip ROM 76.6 deg in RHE) -> 75 deg start. Facts and checks: research/reverse_hyperextension.json.
